pr_title: Display correct symbol in warning when unique name is used without @onready annotation
pr_body:
Closes #102386.

This adds a few lines of code to the procedure generating the warning. It simply checks if the path being used in shorthand begins with "%", and if so uses that symbol instead of "$" for the warning.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cbd3e4a-0fa5-4d4b-8106-198c2e157cd9
pr_comments: Tests have been added! They're in the same file as the existing tests for the `GET_NODE_DEFAULT_WITHOUT_ONREADY` warning, since this PR's addition is just a variant of those.

issue_context.title: "The default value is using "$" which won't return nodes..." warning despite using Unique Name ("%")
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.4.beta.custom_build [eee39f004]

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta (eee39f004) - macOS Sequoia (15.3.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon Pro 5500 XT OpenGL Engine - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700K CPU @ 3.80GHz (16 threads)

### Issue description

The error message for attempting to access a unique-named node in a class body without the `@onready` annotation is slightly incorrect - it claims the user is using "$", when in reality the user is using "%".

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ba9b6f5-1bf6-40f2-a5a8-1ab799010175)

 

### Steps to reproduce

In a new GDScript file, on the class level, type the following:
```gdscript
var something = %Hello
```

You will get an error like
```
The default value is using "$" which won't return nodes in the scene tree before "_ready()" is called. Use the "@onready" annotation to solve this. (Warning treated as error.)gdscript(-1)
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A

review_comments: There are 2 variables: `is_get_node` and `is_using_shorthand`. Are you sure that this is the correct one?

My understanding was that `is_using_shorthand` was used for when the `$` or `%` prefix was used, rather than a call to the `get_node` method:
```gdscript
# In all of these, is_get_node = true
var a = get_node("Node2D")  # is_using_shorthand = false
var b = $Node2D             # is_using_shorthand = true
var c = %Node2D             # is_using_shorthand = true
```
Since in all of these cases, `is_get_node` is `true`, we start out by checking it - then, we change the string to output to one of the shorthand versions if `is_using_shorthand` is `true` as well.
